# Create full video playthroughs

## Problem statement

`npm run capture` records a **fixed-length** clip (default 15 s) driven by a
wall-clock scripted key plan, so it can never show a whole run: it starts
mid-menu and stops arbitrarily, long before any victory or defeat screen. We
need the capture routine to record a **complete game from the start of play to
the end of the run** — across however many levels that run spans — and to keep
recording for **5 seconds after the victory or defeat moment**.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants a single command that
  produces a full, shareable playthrough video (demo / marketing / release
  evidence) without hand-holding the recorder.
  - *As the maintainer, I run `npm run capture` once and get a video of a
    complete run, from Play Game to 5 s past the victory or defeat screen.*
- **Secondary — future CI / QA.** Wants a repeatable full-run clip as
  regression evidence (the run length varies, so the tooling must detect the
  end rather than assume a duration).
- **Tertiary — the shipped-game player.** Benefits indirectly: the in-game
  demo/attract lifecycle must pause briefly on the game-over screen so an
  onlooker (and the capture) can see the outcome before it loops.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` boots Vite + headless Chromium, presses
  Enter, replays a **fixed-duration** plan from `scripts/capture-bot.mjs`
  (`buildScriptedPlan` / `BASE_SWEEP_PATTERN`), records the canvas via
  `canvas.captureStream(60)` + `MediaRecorder`, and probes the clip for
  non-triviality.
- There is **no end-of-run detection**: the recorder stops when the plan's
  hold time elapses (`--duration`, default `DEFAULT_CAPTURE_DURATION_MS =
  15_000`).
- A run ends when the boss dies (victory) or the player runs out of lives
  (defeat): `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_finishRun(won)` calls
  `scene.start('GameOverScene', { won, score })`; `src/core/GameState.ts`
  `defeatBoss()` / `playerDied()` set `gameState = 'gameover'`.
- The shipped game exposes **no page-side signal** for that transition — the
  capture only has the canvas.
- The in-game demo/attract mode does **not exist yet**; it is tracked by
  Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene
  (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) and Capture tooling records the in-game demo
  (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V), both currently `blocked`. Per its AC3 the demo
  lifecycle returns to the menu / restarts when a run ends.
- Existing capture harness: `scripts/capture-progress.mjs` (progress/ETA) and
  hermetic tests in `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **End-of-run signal (Q1A).** The game emits a small **read-only page-side
   signal** when a run ends — a `CustomEvent` on `window` (e.g.
   `aihell:run-ended` with `{ won, score }`) and/or a
   `window.__aiHellRunState` flag set on the `GameOverScene` transition. It
   must be additive/dev-gated so the shipped bundle and normal play are
   unaffected.
2. **Full-run capture (Q2A).** `npm run capture` records one run from the
   start of play (Play Game / demo entry) through **every level that run
   spans** to the first game over, then keeps recording for a configurable
   **tail of 5 000 ms** after the signal before stopping — for **both** a
   victory and a defeat.
3. **Safety cap.** A `--max-duration` bound (generous default) stops the
   recording if no end-of-run signal arrives, so a stuck run cannot record
   forever; hitting the cap is reported explicitly.
4. **Demo dwell (Q3A).** In demo mode, hold on the game-over screen for a
   configurable dwell (≥ 5 s, i.e. ≥ the capture tail) before returning to
   the menu / restarting, so the captured tail shows the victory/defeat
   screen. Normal (non-demo) play is unchanged.
5. **Backwards compatibility.** The explicit fixed-length mode
   (`--duration`) and the scripted-plan path remain available; only the
   default behaviour for `npm run capture` becomes the full-run capture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (signal):** A run ending in victory or defeat emits a documented,
  read-only page-side signal (`aihell:run-ended` `CustomEvent` on `window`
  and/or `window.__aiHellRunState`) containing the outcome. The signal is
  additive: normal play and the shipped bundle are unaffected, and it fires
  for **both** outcomes.
- **AC2 (full capture):** `npm run capture` records a complete run from the
  start of play through all levels to the first game over, then continues
  recording for the configurable tail (default 5 000 ms) after the signal,
  and stops. Verified for a victory path and a defeat path.
- **AC3 (safety cap):** A configurable `--max-duration` cap bounds the
  recording; when the cap is hit without an end signal the tool reports it
  clearly and exits non-zero (a capped clip is not silently presented as a
  complete run). `--tail <ms>` configures the post-signal tail.
- **AC4 (demo dwell):** In demo mode the game-over screen dwells for a
  configurable period of at least the capture tail before the demo loops or
  returns to the menu; non-demo play is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **AC5 (tests):** Hermetic unit tests cover: decoding the end-of-run signal
  payload, the tail/cap calculations, and the demo-dwell decision; an
  integration test asserts that a stubbed end-of-run signal stops the
  recording after the tail. Existing capture tests continue to pass.
- **AC6 (documentation):** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the
  `README.md` capture section document the new default full-run behaviour,
  `--max-duration` / `--tail`, the end-of-run signal, and the demo dwell,
  including code comments for the new signal and constant.
- **AC7 (suite):** Full project test suite (`npm test`), `npm run build` and
  `npm run typecheck` all pass with the new changes. (CHANGELOG is managed by
  the ship skill and is excluded.)

## Constraints

- **Dependency:** blocked by the in-game demo engine
  (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) and Capture tooling records the in-game demo
  (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V); the run is captured via demo mode.
- **Opt-in tooling:** capture stays outside the shipped bundle; the only
  `src/` addition is the small, additive end-of-run signal (dev-gated) and
  the demo dwell.
- **Testability:** the browser/encode path cannot run under vitest (the
  canvas is stubbed), so all new decision logic (signal decoding, tail/cap,
  dwell) must be pure and unit-tested; the browser path is exercised by
  `npm run capture`.
- **Non-deterministic runs:** the game is not fully deterministic (unseeded
  wave/spawn RNG), so the run length varies and the design must rely on the
  end-of-run signal, never on an assumed duration.
- **Cost:** long runs mean longer wall-clock and larger WebM files; the cap
  and progress heartbeat must make this visible and bounded.
- **Backwards compatibility:** `--duration` (fixed length) and the scripted
  fallback remain functional.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — wait for the end signal, record the tail, enforce the cap; report outcome
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — pure helpers for end-signal decoding / tail+cap logic (co-located with existing pure predicates)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — unit tests for the new pure helpers
- `scripts/capture-progress.mjs` — progress/heartbeat across an unbounded (capped) recording
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — emit the end-of-run signal in `_finishRun`; demo-mode game-over dwell
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — outcome available for the signal (if emitted here instead)
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — `gameover` / `bossDefeated` outcome source
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — document full-run capture, signal, cap, dwell
- `README.md` — update the capture command section

## Related work

- Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic… (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ) — parent epic (`plan_complete`); this work extends its capture/demo pipeline.
- Capture tooling records the in-game demo (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V) — sibling; **blocks** this item (capture must first record the demo).
- Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) — sibling; **blocks** this item (provides the demo run and the lifecycle to dwell on game over).
- Documentation for attract/demo mode and bot (AH-0MUX4975J0045VDZ) — sibling; capture documentation must stay consistent with it.
- Spike: automated gameplay video capture (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK) — the pipeline this builds on.
- Scripted Gameplay Videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC) — related `idea`: multi-scene scripted video (fades between scenes); distinct from a single full-run capture, but shares the capture harness.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MTEI0XRD0042ZEZ** – Write AC2+AC3: smooth return and no jump tests (completed)
- **AH-0MUNR5LM1004B223** – Add wave-timeout to all enemy gyms (except boss) (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYTPMC002GLEJ** – Add bullet TTL to enemy configurator (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: adjust, capture, captures, complete, create, ending, full, game, moment, npm, past, present, run, seconds, should, video
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: adjust, capture, complete, create, defeat, ending, full, game, moment, npm, present, run, seconds, should
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: capture, captures, complete, create, ending, full, game, npm, present, run, seconds, should

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the demo engine (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) will own the run lifecycle; this item adds only the dwell, coordinated with that item. If the demo engine instead already holds on game over, the dwell becomes a no-op/config.
- **Risk (signal race):** the run could end before the capture attaches its listener. *Mitigation:* install the listener via `page.addInitScript` before the game boots, and read the `window.__aiHellRunState` flag as a fallback.
- **Risk (production signal):** a `window` event in shipped code. *Mitigation:* gate it to the dev/test build (`import.meta.env.DEV`) or make it provably inert, and verify `npm run check-bundle` still passes.
- **Risk (long run):** high wall-clock and large files on a full victory run. *Mitigation:* `--max-duration` cap, visible heartbeat, and documented cost in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.
- **Risk (headless stability):** long headless WebGL/MediaRecorder sessions may drop frames or fail. *Mitigation:* probe still gates non-triviality; document the run-time expectation.
- **Assumption:** the tail should show the game-over screen, hence the demo dwell; if the operator later prefers the menu in the tail, the dwell can be removed.
- **Scope-creep risk:** multi-scene scripted videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC), MP4 export, and full determinism are **out of scope** — link them as separate work items rather than widening this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — How should capture detect the run's end (victory/defeat)?**
  - **Answer (Map, interactive reply):** **A** — add a small read-only page-side signal (a DOM `CustomEvent` / `window.__aiHellRunState`) emitted by the game when a run ends.
  - Options A (page-side signal) / B (expose dev-only game instance) / C (canvas OCR). Recommended A.
- **Q2 — What does "a complete game" mean, and when does recording stop?**
  - **Answer (Map, interactive reply):** **A**, with the clarification that it is **start → 5 seconds after the game ends in victory or defeat**, and the run **may span more than one level** (it is a whole run, not a fixed level). A safety cap is accepted.
  - Options A (one run, win or lose, +5 s tail) / B (victory only, retry on defeat) / C (multiple attract-loop runs). Recommended A.
- **Q3 — Sequencing vs the demo-mode epic, and the 5 s tail.**
  - **Answer (Map, interactive reply):** **A** — sequence this item after the demo-mode epic; the demo holds on the game-over screen for a configurable dwell (≥ 5 s) so the captured tail is meaningful. Record `blocked-by` dependencies on the demo engine and the demo-capture sibling.
  - Options A (sequence after epic + demo dwell) / B (implement now on scripted bot) / C (record demo without changing lifecycle). Recommended A.

No OPEN QUESTIONs remain.


## Plan (2026-10-07)

Decomposed into six child work items (dependency order). The design keeps all
new decision logic pure and browser-free so it is hermetic and unit-tested,
while the shipped-game addition is limited to the additive, dev-gated
end-of-run signal and the demo game-over dwell.

### Child work items (dependency order)

1. **Run-end signal, tail and dwell helpers** (AH-0MUXZ49PY0065K2O) — no
   dependencies. Test-first foundation: the pure contracts for decoding the
   run-ended payload, the tail/cap arithmetic, the cap-hit decision and the
   demo dwell, with unit tests. Parent AC5.
2. **Emit dev-gated end-of-run signal** (AH-0MUXZ4BXK001QCEK) — depends on 1.
   `PlayScene._finishRun` emits `aihell:run-ended` and sets
   `window.__aiHellRunState`, both outcomes, `import.meta.env.DEV`-gated.
   Parent AC1.
3. **Demo-mode game-over dwell** (AH-0MUXZ4CAE008QRFZ) — depends on 1. Demo
   holds on the game-over screen for `DEMO_GAME_OVER_DWELL_MS` (>= tail),
   non-scoring, before returning to the menu. Parent AC4.
4. **Full-run capture wait, tail and cap** (AH-0MUXZ4CNS009RV40) — depends on
   1, 2. Default `npm run capture` waits for the signal (init-script listener
   + flag fallback), records `--tail` (default 5000 ms), enforces
   `--max-duration`, and fails non-zero on a cap hit. Parent AC2/AC3.
5. **Full-run capture integration verification** (AH-0MUXZ4D0M001IWW1) —
   depends on 3, 4. Stubbed-signal integration tests (victory + defeat + cap),
   dwell-vs-tail check, and green `npm test` / `npm run build` /
   `npm run typecheck`. Parent AC5/AC7.
6. **Document full-run capture and dwell** (AH-0MUXZ4DDV0098ZW4) — depends on
   2, 3, 4. `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and `README.md`. Parent AC6.

### Vertical slice phasing

Each child is an end-to-end increment (code + tests where applicable):
pure contracts → in-game signal → demo dwell → capture loop → integration
verification → documentation. Between phases, review and update the next
child's description before starting it.

### Test-first ordering

Child 1 lands the pure-function contracts and their failing/passing unit
tests before the wiring children consume them. Children 3 and 4 add their own
unit tests; child 5 provides the stubbed end-to-end integration verification.

### Plan-run clarifications

No new interview questions were required: the intake Appendix (Q1-Q3) already
answers the end-of-run detection, the meaning of "complete run" and the
sequencing vs the demo epic. Two **implementation** choices remain for the
producer, each with a recommended option (recorded as OPEN QUESTIONs, not
blocking):

- **OPEN QUESTION (dwell mechanism):** the demo engine (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY)
  currently **skips `GameOverScene`** on game over for its non-scoring rule, so
  AC4 ("the game-over screen dwells...") needs a demo-safe game-over display.
  *Recommended:* start `GameOverScene` from the demo with `{ demo: true }`,
  render VICTORY/DEFEAT + score without leaderboard qualification or initials,
  and auto-return to the menu after the dwell. Alternative: an outcome overlay
  held in `PlayScene`. Directed to the producer during plan review.
- **OPEN QUESTION (signal transport):** prefer the `CustomEvent` alone, the
  `window.__aiHellRunState` flag alone, or both. *Recommended:* both, with the
  flag as the race fallback (matches the parent risk mitigation). Directed to
  the producer during plan review.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-07: Initial planning session (downtime dispatch). Pre-check `plan`
  (Small/Medium); approval gate returned `request_approval: false`. Created six
  child work items with dependency edges (contracts → signal → {dwell, capture}
  → verification → docs). Ran the six automated review stages and the AC
  coverage review (100%, `proceed`). Recorded the plan block and two
  producer-facing OPEN QUESTIONs; stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Summary

The demo bot has no clear goals — its movement looks random because the decision ladder puts "engage the nearest threat" above collection, so the ship chases whichever enemy/asteroid is nearest and changes direction constantly. The operator wants a fixed, legible goal order for the bot's **movement** decisions:

1. **Collect minerals**
2. **Collect power-ups**
3. **Shoot enemies**
4. **Shoot asteroids**

Survival remains the hard constraint (the bot must never deliberately fly into a bullet, hazard or wall), but among safe directions it must pursue the goal above.

## Desired behaviour

`decideBotInput` selects its movement target by this fixed priority when the direction toward it is safe:

1. Nearest **mineral** within `mineralSeekRange` → steer to collect it.
2. Else nearest **power-up drop** within `powerUpSeekRange` → steer to collect it.
3. Else nearest **live enemy** (non-asteroid; the boss counts as an enemy) within `engagementRadius` → steer to engage/aim at it.
4. Else nearest **live asteroid** within `engagementRadius` → steer to engage/aim at it.
5. Else idle (hold station).

The existing survival tier (wall margin, hazard keep-away, reactive + predictive bullet avoidance, fire-tell avoidance) still runs first and bounds every choice, and the human-like input governor (AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB) still rate-limits the committed input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: With a mineral and a power-up in range, the bot steers to the mineral (minerals outrank power-ups).
- AC2: With a power-up and a live enemy in range (no mineral), the bot steers to the power-up.
- AC3: With live enemies and a live asteroid in range (no picks), the bot steers to the enemy (enemies outrank asteroids).
- AC4: With only a live asteroid in range, the bot steers to the asteroid.
- AC5: The survival tier still overrides goal-seeking — the bot never chooses a direction that flies into a bullet/hazard/wall when a safe direction exists.
- AC6: The bot keeps the danger margin when engaging (backs away from a target inside `dangerMargin`).
- AC7: Targeted decisions are deterministic and pure (same snapshot → same input).
- AC8: The decision-ladder docs (module header, README, GDD) describe the new order; docs-assertion tests pass.
- AC9: Full suite, typecheck and build pass.

- AC10: The bot plans its stopping distance ahead: when continuing to thrust
  would overshoot the target (the current speed cannot be shed by friction
  within the remaining distance), it stops thrusting (coasts) and resumes only
  once it can stop in time. It arrives at collection targets and the
  engagement standoff without flying past them.

## Notes

- This **supersedes the parent epic's movement priority** (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ AC2): minerals now outrank power-ups, and collection outranks enemy/asteroid engagement. Survival (epic AC4, never-suicide) and fire-pattern avoidance (epic AC3) are unchanged.
- The human-like governor from AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB is unchanged and still applies on top.

## Related work

discovered-from:AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ (Smart capture bot). Supersedes its AC2 movement order.

## Operator review follow-up (2026-10-07)

The producer reports the bot still "tends to overshoot with its thrusters" and
"needs to plan further into the future". The decision now accounts for the
ship's Newtonian stopping distance (a forward model of its own momentum):
thrusting is suppressed when the remaining distance to the target is shorter
than the distance needed to shed the current speed by friction. This is
tracked as **AC10**.

## Operator review follow-up #2 (2026-10-07) — SUPERSEDES AC1–AC4

The producer reports the bot is **too eager to chase single minerals** and
strays from combat. Because more minerals drop when asteroids/enemies are
destroyed, chasing a lone scattered mineral is a net loss; and the primary
objective is to clear the wave before the 30 s timer expires (survivors carry
over otherwise). The fixed "minerals → power-ups → enemies → asteroids"
ladder (AC1–AC4) is therefore **superseded** by a willingness/utility model:
enemies are the default objective and pickups must *earn* a diversion.

New requirements:

- **AC11 — grouped minerals only.** The bot only diverts to a mineral when it
  belongs to a **cluster** (>= `mineralGroupMinSize` minerals close together);
  a lone mineral never diverts it from engaging enemies.
- **AC12 — distance falls off.** Willingness to divert to a mineral cluster
  decreases with distance; a far cluster no longer diverts while a near one
  does.
- **AC13 — upgrades are a little more diverting.** A power-up drop gets a
  higher willingness than a lone mineral, so a nearby upgrade diverts while a
  lone (or far) mineral does not.
- **AC14 — clear the wave before the timer.** The bot aims to destroy all
  live non-asteroid enemies before the wave timer expires; as the timer runs
  down it raises the diversion threshold (stops detouring) and focuses fire on
  the remaining enemies.

The survival tier, precise aiming, forward-model braking and human-like
governor are unchanged and still apply.

## Notes

- This **supersedes the parent epic's movement priority** (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ AC2) and this item's AC1–AC4: enemies (wave clear) are the default objective, and grouped minerals / upgrades are opportunistic diversions that must out-weigh the wave-clear threshold. Survival (epic AC4, never-suicide) and fire-pattern avoidance (epic AC3) are unchanged.

## Operator review follow-up #3 (2026-10-07)

The producer is happy with the utility model but reports the bot **does not
hold the thrust key long enough** — it toggles the thruster "on/off/on/off"
(an artefact of the per-tick forward-model braking reflex). A human would
press for a perceptible burst. Each thrust press must be **extended by a
random 25–60%** for a human feel.

- **AC15 — human-like thrust presses.** When the bot presses forward thrust,
  it holds the key for at least a base press duration extended by a random
  **+25% to +60%** (drawn per press). Single-tick "blips" are therefore
  extended into real presses; the steering cadence and the braking behaviour
  are otherwise unchanged. The randomness is deterministic for a given run
  seed (press durations are reproducible per run).

## Operator review follow-up #4 (2026-10-07)

Producer: "Reduce the longer end of the press to 225 unless the bot is wanting
to travel further, in which case let it go up to 400ms. When travelling
further distances, if the bot is going to overshoot then have it spin approx
180 and use thrusters in the other direction."

- **AC16 — conditional press cap.** The forward-thrust press is drawn from
  **200–225 ms** normally; when the chosen target is far
  (`>= longTravelDistance`) the upper bound extends to **400 ms** so long legs
  get longer bursts.
- **AC17 — hard retro-brake.** When the bot is moving fast
  (`>= retroBrakeMinSpeed`) and the forward model says coasting cannot stop it
  in time (it would overshoot), it no longer just coasts: it **spins ~180°**
  (intent heading opposite its current velocity) and **thrusts in the opposite
  direction** to brake, then resumes the approach once it can stop in time.

Both remain deterministic per run seed; the survival tier still bounds the
brake direction.

## Operator review follow-up #5 (2026-10-07) — AC17 RETRACTED

Producer: "Don't use the 180 retro brake, it breaks everything."

**AC17 (the hard 180° retro-brake) is withdrawn.** The bot returns to AC10
forward-model braking only: when continuing to thrust would overshoot it
suppresses the thrust and **coasts** (no spin, no reverse thrust).
`retroBrakeMinSpeed` and the `retroBrakeIntent` code path are removed.

**AC16 is retained**: the forward-thrust press is 200–225 ms normally, extended
to 400 ms when the chosen target is a long-travel leg (`>= longTravelDistance`);
`longTravelDistance` and the intent's `longTravel` press-cap flag remain.

## Summary
Replace the per-frame priority ladder with a **bot framework**: a world model, a registry of goals/behaviours, a committed policy and a content configuration seam. This is the maintainable core that later content and styles plug into.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A `BotBrain`/policy interface that maps a `BotSnapshot` (+ world model + memory) to an input, with an explicit **commitment** mechanism (a selected goal is held until achieved, invalidated, or outranked by a margin for a minimum time).
- AC2: A **goal/behaviour registry**: goals and behaviours register by id; adding one does not require editing the core switch/if-chain.
- AC3: A world-model/predictor layer (positions/velocities, incoming-fire prediction) separated from decision policy, so prediction is testable in isolation.
- AC4: The existing pure `decideBotInput` is preserved behind an adapter (so current tests/gyms keep working) or cleanly superseded with documented parity tests.
- AC5: The framework is deterministic and pure over an injected `dt`/clock; no wall-clock dependence.
- AC6: Unit tests: registry, commitment/hysteresis, deterministic replay of a decision sequence.
- AC7: Docs: framework overview + how goals/behaviours are structured.
data.title: Bot framework core: world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy

# Demo mode: ESC returns to the main menu; only movement keys take over

*In attract/demo mode, only ESC and the movement keys (W/A/S/D or arrows) should affect the run: ESC returns to the main menu, a movement key hands control to the player in place, and every other key and the pointer are ignored.*

## Problem statement

In attract/demo mode, **any** keyboard key or pointer press currently hands control to the player in place (`setDemoMode(false)`). This is far too sensitive for an unattended attract loop: an accidental keypress or a stray click silently drops the demo into human control instead of keeping the bot playing. The operator wants only deliberate, gameplay-relevant input to affect the demo — **ESC** to leave to the main menu, and the **movement keys** (W/A/S/D or the arrow keys) to take over as normal play. All other input must be ignored.

## Users

- **As an arcade operator running the attract loop**, I want the demo to keep playing unattended so that stray keypresses or mouse activity do not silently drop it into human control.
- **As a player who has just watched the demo**, I want to press a movement key (W/A/S/D or an arrow key) to take over and keep playing the current run.
- **As a player or operator who wants to leave the demo**, I want to press ESC to return cleanly to the main menu.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I leave the cabinet unattended in demo mode; someone bumps a random key/property the mouse, and the demo keeps playing as if nothing happened.
- As a player, the demo is running and I press **W** or the **up arrow** — I am now in control of the ship mid-run, exactly as before.
- As a player, the demo is running and I press **ESC** — I land back on the main menu.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — ESC returns to the main menu.** While `PlayScene` is in demo mode, pressing **ESC** returns directly to `MenuScene`. It must **not** take over the run and must **not** open the pause menu. ESC in non-demo play continues to toggle the pause menu, unchanged.
2. **AC2 — Movement keys take over.** While in demo mode, pressing a **movement key** — W/A/S/D (using the player's configured `moveUp`/`moveDown`/`moveLeft`/`moveRight` bindings) or an **arrow key** — calls `setDemoMode(false)` in place; the run continues and the keyboard then drives the ship. Rebinding movement keys is honoured.
3. **AC3 — All other input is ignored.** While in demo mode, any other keyboard key (e.g. Space, Enter, Tab, letters/numbers, function keys) is ignored and the demo keeps playing; the **pointer/click no longer takes over**. (Pointer-ignored is an explicit assumption — see Risks; ESC is the only non-movement special case.)
4. **AC4 — Unattended demo lifecycle unchanged.** With no input, a demo run still plays to completion and follows the existing demo lifecycle (auto `GameOverScene` demo dwell → return to the menu, non-scoring). Narrowing the take-over must not affect this path.
5. **AC5 — Normal play unaffected.** Outside demo mode no take-over listener is registered; ESC still toggles pause; keyboard and pointer behaviour are byte-for-byte unchanged.
6. **AC6 — Tests.** Automated tests cover: ESC returns to `MenuScene`; a movement key takes over; a non-movement key does not take over; the pointer does not take over; ESC does not pause while demoing; normal play is unaffected; listeners are cleaned up on take-over, ESC-exit and shutdown.
7. **AC7 — Documentation.** README (attract/demo section), the Game Design Document attract/demo subsection and the affected code comments are updated to describe ESC → main menu and movement-key take-over.
8. **AC8 — Quality gates.** Typecheck and build pass, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Demo-only change.** Only the demo/attract path may change behaviour; normal play must be unchanged (AC5).
- **Gym↔game parity.** Take-over/demo mode is `PlayScene`-only (gyms have no demo mode); no divergence is expected. Confirm no shared-core (`src/scenes/core/`) change is required; if one is, apply it consistently.
- **Single source of movement keys.** Derive the take-over key set from the same source as normal play (`this.cursors` arrow keys + the resolved `moveUp`/`moveDown`/`moveLeft`/`moveRight` bindings produced by `_applyBindings()`), so custom bindings are honoured.
- **ESC/pause arbitration.** The existing ESC → `togglePause()` handler must not also fire while demo mode is on; exactly one ESC action (return to menu) applies in demo.
- **No new dependencies.**

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
  - `_enableDemoTakeOver()` (~line 2264) registers a broad `this.input.keyboard?.on('keydown', handler)` **and** `this.input.on('pointerdown', handler)`, both calling `this.setDemoMode(false)` in place.
  - `_disableDemoTakeOver()` (~line 2280) removes those listeners; called on take-over, on `setDemoMode(false)`, in `_finishRun` and on shutdown (no cross-session leak).
  - `create()` registers ESC → `this.togglePause()` (~lines 560–565); demo mode does not override it, so today ESC during a demo opens the pause menu.
  - `setDemoMode(demo)` (public) turns demo on/off and enables/disables take-over.
  - Movement keys: `this.cursors = this.input.keyboard.createCursorKeys()` and `this.wasd` built in `_applyBindings()` from the resolved settings bindings.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — `startDemo()` starts `PlayScene` with `{ demo: true }`; the idle-attract timer restarts the demo after 15 s of menu inactivity.
- Docs describing the current "any key or pointer takes over" behaviour: `README.md` (~line 363 and the run instructions ~line 386) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §**Attract / demo mode**, line 159 ("**Take over:** pressing any key or the pointer leaves demo mode in place").

## Desired change

- Replace the broad demo take-over listeners in `PlayScene` with:
  - an **ESC handler active only in demo mode** that returns to `MenuScene` (e.g. `this.scene.start('MenuScene')`) — it must not pause;
  - a **narrow `keydown` handler** that takes over (`setDemoMode(false)`) only when the pressed key is a movement key (arrow key or the configured movement binding);
  - **no `pointerdown` take-over**.
- Suppress / bypass the normal ESC → `togglePause()` path while demo mode is on so only the return-to-menu action runs.
- Keep the existing cleanup semantics (rename `_enableDemoTakeOver`/`_disableDemoTakeOver` only if it improves clarity), so no listener leaks across take-over, run end or shutdown.
- Update the README and GDD attract/demo text, and the affected code comments, to the new behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **Edit**: narrow movement-key take-over, demo ESC → `MenuScene`, suppress pause-ESC in demo, listener cleanup.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — **Edit**: unit tests for ESC→menu, pause suppression, movement-key take-over, non-movement-key ignored, pointer ignored, cleanup.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` — **Edit**: adjust/extend the existing demo take-over test (currently `ArrowLeft`, a movement key — still valid) and add a non-movement-key no-op case if appropriate.
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — **Edit**: integration coverage that ESC returns to the live `MenuScene`, a movement key takes over, and other input is a no-op.
- `README.md` — **Edit**: attract/demo description (line 363) and the "press any key to take over" run instruction (line 386).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **Edit**: attract/demo subsection, "Take over" bullet (line 159).

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- **ESC/pause double-fire (medium).** If both the demo ESC handler and the existing pause handler fire, ESC could open the pause menu and/or return to the menu. Mitigation: gate `togglePause()` on `!this.demoMode` (or route ESC through one handler) and assert both outcomes in tests.
- **Key-matching correctness (medium).** Matching a `KeyboardEvent` by `event.key` is layout/rebind sensitive. Mitigation: compare against the same resolved bindings/arrow keys used for movement, and cover rebinds where practical.
- **Test churn (low).** Existing tests assert the broad take-over (e.g. `MenuScene.test.ts` "pressing a control during the demo takes over" uses `ArrowLeft` — a movement key, so it stays valid; check `demoMode.integration.test.ts` for pointer take-over assertions).
- **Choice-overlay edge case (low).** While the hold-full `MineralChoiceScene` overlay is open in a demo run (`PlayScene` paused, overlay launched), keyboard events may still reach `PlayScene`'s listeners. The narrowed handlers must not misfire there; the existing bot auto-select (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`) already unsticks the demo. Verify ESC/movement keys during the overlay do not break the overlay or the run.
- **Attract-loop restart (low).** After ESC → menu, the 15 s idle-attract timer restarts, so the demo restarts if left untouched. This is existing menu behaviour, not a regression.
- **Scope-creep (low).** Re-adding take-over on additional keys, changing the pause model, or altering capture tooling are **out of scope**; record any such opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

**Assumptions (producer-validatable)**

- The **pointer is ignored** in demo mode — the operator listed only ESC plus W/A/S/D/arrow keys, so a stray click should not stop the demo. (One-line change to restore pointer take-over if this is wrong.)
- ESC returns to the menu **immediately**, abandoning the demo run without the game-over dwell or any scoring.
- Disabling pause while demoing is acceptable — pausing an unattended demo is not meaningful, and ESC already means "leave the demo".
- The take-over key set is the **movement keys only** (arrow keys + configured movement bindings), including S / down, since that is what "movement keys" means to the player even though the bot itself never reverses.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUX4966Z0009P9Q** — Attract/demo entry point in MenuScene — *completed*. Introduced the press-to-take-over behaviour (AC3) that this item narrows.
- **AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY** — Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene — *completed*. Owns `setDemoMode`/`getBotInput` and the demo lifecycle.
- **AH-0MUXZ4CAE008QRFZ** — Demo-mode game-over dwell — *completed*. The unattended demo return path that AC4 preserves.
- **AH-0MUY4881P007FJ8R** — Bot still controls the player after Watch Demo then Play Game — *completed*. The start-data contract; interaction with ESC→menu must be checked.
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ** — Smart capture bot (parent epic) — *completed*. Parent of the demo-mode work.
- **AH-0MUX4975J0045VDZ** — Documentation for attract/demo mode and bot — *completed*. Prior documentation that AC7 updates.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What input should take over / exit the demo?** (Options: (a) ignore everything except ESC; (b) ignore non-ESC keys but keep pointer take-over.) Answer (operator): *"ESC but let AWSD or arrow keys allow the player to take control"* — i.e. keep take-over but only on movement keys; ESC is the only exit. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — What should ESC do during the demo, given ESC already toggles the pause menu?** (Options: (a) return directly to the main menu with pause disabled while demoing; (b) ESC opens pause, second ESC returns to menu.) Answer (operator): (a). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Keep a take-over path at all?** (Options: (a) remove take-over entirely; (b) keep it on an explicit key.) Answer (operator): *"see 1"* — keep take-over, bound to movement keys only. Source: interactive reply.
- **Assumption A1 — pointer behaviour.** The operator's answer to Q1 named only keyboard movement keys, so the pointer is treated as ignored in demo mode. Marked as an assumption to be validated; trivially reversible. Source: inference from Q1 (not separately confirmed).

data.description:
Demo take-over: narrow to movement keys only, ESC to main menu, suppress pointer.

Replace the broad demo take-over with narrow handlers:
- ESC: return to MenuScene (suppresses togglePause while demoing)
- Movement keys (arrows + configured WASD): setDemoMode(false) in place
- Pointer: no longer takes over (removed pointerdown listener)
- All other input: ignored

Implementation plan:

1. _enableDemoTakeOver() - narrow handlers
Replace the current broad keydown + pointerdown listeners with a single keydown
handler that branches on the key:
  - ESC -> this.scene.start('MenuScene'), then _disableDemoTakeOver()
  - Movement key (arrow keys + wasd bindings) -> setDemoMode(false)
  - Everything else -> ignored (no-op)
Remove the pointerdown listener entirely.

2. _isMovementKey(event) - movement key check
Derive from the same source as normal play:
  - Arrow keys: ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right
  - Configured bindings: this.wasd values (set in _applyBindings from resolved settings)
  - Also this.cursors (Phaser cursor keys)
The wasd dictionary maps W/A/S/D to the resolved key strings. We check wasd
values plus the four arrow key strings.

3. ESC/pause arbitration
The existing ESC togglePause handler in create() fires on every ESC. Prevent
it from toggling pause while demoing by gating:
  if (event.key === this.pauseKeyName && !event.repeat && !this.demoMode)
    this.togglePause();
Then the demo ESC handler is the only ESC action during demo.

4. Cleanup
_disableDemoTakeOver() already removes registered listeners. On ESC to menu,
call _disableDemoTakeOver() before scene.start('MenuScene').

Files changed:
- src/scenes/PlayScene.ts (core logic)
- Tests in PlayScene.test.ts, demoMode.integration.test.ts, MenuScene.test.ts
- README.md, docs/Game Design Document.md
